Guidance & outlook: So FY27, we are sticking to our guidance of INR700 crores.
Just one thing, just to reiterate, your FY27 guidance is about INR700 crores.

So going forward, can we look at some big ticket orders, let's say, INR150 crores to INR200 crores worth of orders so that we can grow our order book to a substantial amount that going forward, we can have a meaningful growth even for the subsequent year.
Growth & demand: This pledging of shares by one of the directors is done for a volume of INR 10 crores.
We are targeting an order book of INR100 crores and more only.
Apart from the current unexecuted order book, we are expecting around INR500 crores plus this year also.
Margins & costs: But when a price hike of around 50% or 60% happened in the raw material, that too in the bitumen, which is a major raw material in road laying, will definitely have a hit.
And the operating margins, EBITDA margins about 18% to 20% is workable, given the rise in the fuel prices, etc.
So, if you see this -- I mean, this H2, we have received 19% operating profit margin, but it was 21% last year.
Capex & expansion: And this expansion will have 1% or 2% hit on the profit, which I have disclosed in the earlier calls.
Sir, actually, capex, I think we are having enough of fleets and enough of assets as of now.
Sir, I think we took around INR25 crores, if we are not mistaken, worth of capex.
Balance sheet & cash: Like right now, the debt is the total borrowing amount is INR234 crores on a consolidated basis.
Currently, we have about INR43 crores in long-term borrowings and INR192 crores in short-term borrowings.

And if you continue to maintain trade payables about INR40 crores to INR50 crores odd, imagine the kind of trade receivables that you will have to fund from either debt or equity and that comes only from debt or equity and equity also will be subject to market conditions.
Risks & challenges: Sir, debtor days increased because during this election, the receivables got delayed a little.

And we expected these receivables would be high because of these elections , because people have a tendency not to take risks to get funds from the finance and have it in their accounts for either the highways department or the PWD department.
And there are some inevitable delays, but it is not that alarming.

guidance.t: In fact, if we are increasing this 1% or 2% profit margin directly, we will be able to get further orders also.

So going forward, can we look at some big ticket orders, let's say, INR150 crores to INR200 crores worth of orders so that we can grow our order book to a substantial amount that going forward, we can have a meaningful growth even for the subsequent year.

Guidance & outlook: That remains our major focus in India and we target to achieve 25% to 30% revenue from other states in the next financial year.

So, what we are saying is the INR500 crores standalone is something that we already have an order book for, visibility for and for the consol level INR100 crores that we are targeting, the INR50 to INR100 crores, currently we are waiting for the approvals to come in, post that we will start the billing and the execution work, right?.

So, we are targeting somewhere around instead of talking about the percentage of top line share from road infra and solar EPC, I will just say that we are targeting somewhere around in the next year, we are targeting a minimum of around INR150 crores to INR200 crores top line from solar EPC.
Growth & demand: Our revenue grew by 79% year-on-year to INR195.7 crores.
As of 30 S eptember 2025, our un-executed order book stands at around INR475 crore, and the bid pipeline remains strongly at around INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crore.
If I would have gone 2 %-3% less, I would have had an order book of around INR1,000-1,500 crores in my kitty by now.
Margins & costs: EBITDA increased 87% and stood at INR44.7 crores, with margins improving to 22.9%.
Maintaining strong margins and disciplined wor king capital management will continue to guide our execution as we scale.
So we need to grow good numbers and e ven at a cost of 1 % or 2% lesser bottom line, we are ready to do that.
Capex & expansion: India continues to see one of its strongest infrastructure cycles, supported by a government capex of over INR11.2 lakh crore s for FY '26, around 3.1% of the GDP.
Heavy construction has remained robust and investment in logistics, multimodal transport and industrial corridors continue to rise.
When we are targeting some geographical expansion or something, there may be some decline in what we are getting in our own home ground.
Balance sheet & cash: So, the main reason is INR85 crores being in the balance for trade receivable is because around INR70 crores we did the billing in the month of September.
So, that is the reason why this receivable is standing at around INR85 crores, sir.
